bull_bear.body: Nothing disclosed — no net debt, no dividend, no returns commentary this call. ESG ratings improved (**CareEdge 84/100, CRISIL 66/100**), positioned as best-in-peer-group.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **Pooled-gas withdrawal is the single biggest swing factor.** Removed *after* the peace deal — mgmt called it *"the sudden decision by the government."* Restoration is a hope, not a plan: *"probably some positive news should come shortly on that part **if the Middle East tension is not getting over**"* — i.e. ATGL now needs the crisis to *persist* for the subsidy mechanism to return, an uncomfortable dependency.
2. **Spot at ~15% of volume at peak prices** — direct, un-hedged P&L exposure with no stated timeline to close.
3. **APM allocation structurally declining** — permanent margin headwind, not cyclical.
4. **No margin recovery date.** *"if you ask me to predict... it would be very difficult."*
5. **FY27 EBITDA guide (₹1,500cr) silently unaddressed** — Q1 run-rate implies ~₹1,124cr. Either a miss is coming or a back-loaded recovery must be articulated next quarter.
6. **CNG station build-out slowed sharply** (+5 vs +25) while CNG demand grows ~30% — either capex discipline or execution slippage; mgmt was not asked.
7. **Skilled-manpower shortage** in PNG (gas plumbing/fitting) — mitigated industry-wide via ITI/diploma tie-ups and a new government skill course, but flagged as a real onboarding constraint.
8. **Competition in overlapping CGD areas** acknowledged — pricing set GA-by-GA "on almost everyday basis."
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Sober and noticeably less promotional than Q4FY26 — a **new CEO (Sanjay Pandita)** running his first call, with the sourcing head (Ravindra Desai) doing the analytical heavy lifting and being genuinely transparent on mix, spot % and the NWG formula. But the call was **short (8 pages, ~6 analysts)** and management **withheld PAT, PBT, net debt, capex quantum, EBITDA/scm and all EV economics**, and did not volunteer that the prior FY27 EBITDA guide is off-track. Declining to fabricate a margin-recovery date is honest; not reconciling to the prior guide is not.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The pooled-gas mechanism was withdrawn *because* of peace, not war.** ATGL is now structurally rooting for either full normalisation (cheap LNG) or continued tension (pool restored) — the worst outcome is exactly where it sits: post-deal, pre-supply.
- **NWG is Brent-linked at 12% of the Indian crude basket** — most models treat "domestic gas" as a price shock-absorber; here 62% domestic mix gave far less protection than it appears.
- **Revenue +27% vs volume +13%** ⇒ realisation up ~12% YoY. ATGL *is* passing through, just not fast enough — the gap is roughly the ₹5/SCM cost move.
- **Government now expects fertiliser gas demand to fall post-sowing**, which mgmt believes frees domestic volume for CGD — the quiet, monsoon-seasonal upside nobody models.
- **I&C customer adds at 3x/2x YoY** is the most under-discussed positive on the call; nobody asked what it does to volume mix.
- EV: 3.3mn electrons at 5,306 CP works out to ~620 electrons/CP for the quarter — utilisation is still the unanswered question mgmt itself named as the focus.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Combined strength of Adani Group and TotalEnergies, blending international expertise with local execution
- Digital capability embedded across operations: SOUL unified enterprise digital platform, MyAdaniGas App for customer engagement, IoT-enabled asset monitoring and analytics-driven decision-making (100% share of digital payments)
- Disciplined, phased capital allocation focused on high-return, customer-centric segments with balance-sheet resilience; low leverage (Net Debt to EBITDA at 1.11) and credit rating upgraded to AA+ (stable) by ICRA/CARE/CRISIL, a 2-notch improvement over 5 years
- Over two decades of execution expertise and an expanding, dense authorised network across 34 Geographical Areas
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Rated 'High' in the Company's FY26 risk heat map (R1). CGD operations are subject to regulatory oversight by PNGRB and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; risk arises from inadequate monitoring/tracking of statutory requirements, including non-fulfilment of Minimum Work Programme (MWP) obligations prescribed by PNGRB for Geographical Areas, which could trigger regulatory action or financial penalties.
- Business risk — Rated 'High' in the FY26 risk heat map (R2), owned by the Business Development Team; relates to core CGD business execution and operating environment.
- Competition risk — Rated 'High' in the FY26 risk heat map (R3), owned by the Business Development Team; reflects competitive pressure within the City Gas Distribution and adjacent energy segments.
- Reputational risk — Rated 'High' in the FY26 risk heat map (R8), owned by the CEO's Office team.
- Financial risk — Rated 'Medium' in the FY26 risk heat map (R9), owned by the Finance Team.
- Health and safety risk — Rated 'Medium' in the FY26 risk heat map (R7), owned by Regional Heads and the ESG Team; material given the Company's gas distribution and CNG/PNG station operations.
- Human resource risk — Rated 'Medium' in the FY26 risk heat map (R11), owned by the Human Resource Head.
- Import dependence and commodity/currency volatility — ATGL's gas sourcing is exposed to global crude and LNG price volatility and INR depreciation. The March 2026 conflict in West Asia and closure of the Strait of Hormuz (which carried ~35% of seaborne crude and ~20% of seaborne LNG trade) caused an unprecedented energy supply shock, force majeure declarations by LNG suppliers, and a sharp rise in gas costs (up ~23% YoY), which management cited as the cause of a marginal moderation in FY26 PBT and PAT despite strong volume growth.

latest_quarter.body:
The margin bridge management gave, in their own terms:
- **Sourcing mix:** domestic APM + NWG ≈ **40%**; long-term contracts ≈ **48%**; balance spot. By origin: **domestic ~62%**, **imported RLNG ~38%** (Brent-linked + Henry-Hub-linked).
- **Spot ≈ 15% of total consumption after the curtailment** — this is the bleeding wound.
- **Two cost shocks stacked:** (i) imported RLNG cost up on the West Asia crisis; (ii) **NWG price = 12% of the Indian crude basket**, so Brent >**$107/bbl** dragged the *domestic* leg up too — *"not only the imported RLNG costs have gone up but... the NWG prices also went up, which has impacted overall the gas cost."* NWG ran **>$5/MMBTU**.
- **APM allocation "going slowly down"** — the structural, non-cyclical part of the compression, admitted plainly by the CEO.
- **Mitigation:** move spot exposure into **mid-term** purchases now (*"not on the short term because the prices are elevated for the shorter term"*) and **long-term** contracts once the market stabilises; contracts coming up for renewal.
- **Pricing lever deliberately under-used:** on CNG, *"If you see the arbitrage between petrol and CNG, there is a room, but at the same time, we have to be conscious of fact of bringing more customers on board"* — volume prioritised over margin, again.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (prior):** Rev ₹1,696cr (+16%); EBITDA ₹310cr (+13%, "highest ever"); PAT ₹156cr. FY26 EBITDA ₹1,225cr. Guided FY27: ~18% revenue growth, **EBITDA ~₹1,500cr**, 10,000 EV CP near-term. CNG stations 705, EV CP 5,100, households 1.1mn.
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Rev **₹1,908cr (+27%)**; EBITDA **₹281cr** (~14.7% margin, **down QoQ from ₹310cr**); PAT/PBT **not disclosed**. Volume 303 MMSCM (+13%); CNG +18%, PNG +4%. Stations 707 (**+5 only**), EV CP 5,306 (58MW, electrons +100%), households 11.41 lakh (+38,000), I&C 10,422 (+448). Pooled-gas mechanism **withdrawn**; spot ≈**15%** of volume; Brent >$107; gas cost +₹5/SCM. **CEO changed: Manglani → Sanjay Pandita.** FY27 EBITDA guide of ₹1,500cr **neither reaffirmed nor withdrawn**.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) is EBITDA back above ₹310cr or is the ₹1,500cr FY27 guide formally cut; (2) has pooled gas been restored; (3) spot % below 15%; (4) any mid-term LNG contract actually signed; (5) CNG station adds back toward 25/qtr; (6) PNG adds ≥38,000 held; (7) first-ever ATEL economics disclosure._

outlook.body:
- Expanding Infrastructure and Reach: strengthening the gas distribution network across authorised Geographical Areas, with expanding pipeline infrastructure and increasing customer connectivity central to growth plans
- Diversification and Innovation: investments in EV charging infrastructure, compressed biogas facilities and LNG for transport represent steps toward building a multi-energy ecosystem
- Customer Delight: delivering reliable and affordable energy remains the highest priority, with continued enhancement of service via digital initiatives (Adani Gas Mitra kiosks, QR-based feedback, agentic-AI response)
- Sustained focus on diversified gas sourcing, consumer centricity, operational excellence, digital infrastructure and capital prudence to navigate a volatile ('VUCA') global energy environment
- Transform the SOUL digital platform into an overarching Integrated Business Platform (IBC) covering safety, security, emergency response, sales and asset operations, asset integrity management, logistics, analytics, gas sourcing, customer billing and customer delight
- ATGL maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Since listing, the Board has recommended a broadly flat annual dividend (Rs 27.5 crore, i.e. Rs 0.25 per equity share of Rs 1 face value) each year, which has meant a steadily declining payout ratio as profits have grown (from about 12% of PAT in the first year post-listing to about 4.3% of PAT in FY26), consistent with prioritising reinvestment of internal accruals into network expansion and diversification over distribution. For FY26, the Board does not propose to transfer any amount to General Reserves.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26, ATGL commissioned 9 new City Gas Stations (CGS) and 1 new LCNG facility in newer Geographical Areas recently connected to the national gas grid, taking total operating CGS to 26 and LCNG to 5. Steel pipeline network expanded to 15,572 inch-km and MDPE pipeline to 8,306 km, with domestic PNG connections crossing 10.99 lakh households (1.37 lakh new connections added) and CNG stations reaching 705, including expansion of CODO/DODO models to 140 stations. Through wholly owned subsidiary Adani TotalEnergies E-Mobility Limited (ATEL), the EV charging network grew to 5,100 installed charge points (4,265 energised) across 225+ cities and 22 airports, adding 26 MW of charging capacity during the year to reach 54 MW installed; ATEL's near-term plan is to scale to around 10,000 charge points across key urban and mobility corridors via a calibrated, asset-light BOHO (Build-Operate-Handover) model. Through wholly owned subsidiary Adani TotalEnergies Biomass Limited (ATBL), Phase 1 of the agri-waste-to-CBG plant at Barsana, Uttar Pradesh was commissioned with 10 TPD production capacity (peak production of 7.5 TPD achieved in FY26), expected to ramp up to 11 TPD in FY 2026-27; pre-development work began on municipal solid waste-based CBG projects in Ahmedabad and Rajkot, and the 'Harit Amrit' brand was launched in MP, UP and Gujarat. Joint venture IndianOil-Adani Gas Private Limited (IOAGPL) tied up new debt facilities of approximately Rs 3,100 crore to fund its planned capital expenditure programme and completed a CCD transaction of Rs 1,400 crore, positioning it to accelerate CGD network build-out across new Geographical Areas. Joint venture Smart Meters Technologies Private Limited (SMTPL) operates a gas-meter manufacturing facility at Gangad, near Ahmedabad, with an annual production capacity of approximately 7.2 lakh meters.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government's long-term ambition to raise natural gas's share in India's primary energy mix to 15% by 2030 (from ~6-6.5% currently) continues to guide CGD ecosystem expansion
- India's natural gas demand expected to grow at 8-9% CAGR through 2030, driven by CGD expansion, fertiliser demand and increasing adoption of gas as a transport fuel
- New Geographical Areas are maturing faster than the base: volumes in new GAs grew 32% YoY, with the newer-GA volume mix improving to 38% from 32% in FY25, underscoring growing acceptance of the expanding network
- CNG continues to outpace PNG growth: CNG volumes rose 18% YoY versus ~6% for PNG, on continued network expansion and customer-focused initiatives
- Policy tailwinds expected to accelerate adoption: simplified natural gas pipeline transportation tariffs for home PNG/CNG, CST applicability on interstate gas movement, and state-level CGD policy adoption/VAT rationalisation
- Diversified gas sourcing strategy is management's primary lever to offset gas cost pressure (up ~23% YoY) while maintaining supply continuity across customer segments
- Early-stage investments in e-mobility and compressed biogas are expected to mature as these segments are poised to grow amid the push to reduce reliance on imported energy sources
- A threefold surge in home PNG connection enquiries followed the geopolitical (West Asia) situation, handled via proactive outreach and digital infrastructure
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Volume and revenue are compounding fine (**303 MMSCM, +13% YoY**; revenue **₹1,908cr, +27%**) but the **margin is the whole story**: EBITDA of ₹281cr on 27% revenue growth means operating margin has slid from ~25% to ~15% over 6–8 quarters, and Q1 got worse — the government **withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia "peace deal"**, pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes at a time Brent crossed **$107/bbl**. Management offers no margin-recovery date and explicitly declines to predict one; the recovery thesis rests entirely on external events (Middle East normalising, US/Qatar LNG supply arriving, pooled gas being restored) plus a self-help plan to shift spot exposure into mid-term contracts. Against the FY27 guide given last quarter (**EBITDA ~₹1,500cr**), Q1's ₹281cr is a **~₹1,124cr run-rate — materially behind**.

open.item: ATGL intends to incur capex of about INR900-1,000 crores in FY26, primarily for network creation of the 11th round geographies.
FY27 capex budget higher than FY26 (no rupee number given)
Gas sales volume growth to continue at Q1 pace (~13% YoY)
ATGL guided to around INR1,500 crores of EBITDA in FY27, with EBITDA growth in line with volume growth.
ATGL expects FY27 revenue growth to be the same as achieved in FY26 (~18%), with newer GAs contributing relatively more than existing GAs.
Over the next 2-3 years ATGL expects to spend INR3,500-3,700 crores of capex, largely on core steel network and CNG stations of the 11th round geographies.
ATGL is positioned to support India's vision to raise the share of natural gas in the energy mix to 15% by 2030 through expanded CGD network.
Margins to recover to prior levels once Middle East crisis ends
Domestic PNG household additions per quarter maintained

Consumer-first calibrated pricing: ATGL will not fully pass through higher gas costs, instead leaning on operational excellence and digitalization to protect affordability and widen the consumer base.
Cheaper alternate liquid fuels (LPG/propane) caused slight industrial/commercial volume degrowth (~1% here and there); pricing pressure expected to persist.
Geopolitical tensions in West Asia since late February disrupted global energy markets, causing higher natural gas prices, supply-chain challenges and currency volatility.
Most of the 34 GAs are now connected to mainstream gas supply; the remaining couple of GAs are likely to be connected via city gas station or LCNG plant anytime soon.
ATGL remains on track to achieve its ambition of installing 10,000 EV charging points in the near term (currently 5,100 via subsidiary ATEL) while improving network utilization.
Industry (including ATGL) is engaging policymakers for MSME connection and consumption-linked incentives to voluntarily adopt piped natural gas.
ATGL currently purchases/blends CBG to the tune of ~1% of total consumption against a regulatory blending requirement rising toward 2%.
Jio-BP tie-up to accelerate addition of DODO and CODO CNG stations across all 34 geographical areas and set up EV charging at strategic locations.
ATGL targets maturing CNG infrastructure to 20% or higher penetration in each geographical area.

verdicts.item: Management expects to maintain double-digit CNG volume growth.
verdicts.note: "CNG volumes grew by 17% year-on-year. During the fourth quarter... and 18% for the financial year"; "double-digit growth track record, which we have been maintaining."

verdicts.item: As it builds more CNG stations, ATGL plans to add more CODO and DODO branded outlets as part of its expansion strategy.
verdicts.note: "705 stations, we are very happy to state 140 stations are under the category of CODO... These are our full branded CNG stations."

verdicts.item: Continue building a robust diversified gas sourcing portfolio (APM allocation for CNG down to ~36%, replaced by New Well Gas, HPHT and market-priced RLNG) with calibrated price pass-through to sustain volume growth.
verdicts.note: "85% of our volumes are met from the APM allocation plus HPHT and WG volumes... balance around 16%, we are buying from the market on a spot basis... a diversified portfolio"; "Price has been calibrate…

verdicts.item: ATGL is on track to realize its ambition of installing 10,000 EV charge points (currently nearing 5,000 via subsidiary ATEL).
verdicts.note: "ATEL, our subsidiary company now operates 5,100 EV charge points"; "we remain on track to achieve our ambition of installing 10,000 EV charging points in the near term" - target not yet reached, only…

verdicts.item: ATGL targets 400 CODO/DODO branded CNG stations versus 136 currently, being calibrated so dealers earn a good IRR.
verdicts.note: "140 stations are under the category of CODO" - up from 136 but well short of the 400 target; target not restated. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management guided to healthy growth in CNG stations both in the coming quarter and next year, above the current 680.
verdicts.note: "addition of 25 new CNG stations during the quarter, taking the total network to 705 stations" - growth above the prior 680.

verdicts.item: Existing geographies continue to see double-digit CNG growth (~12%) while newer geographies grow 30%+, sustaining overall double-digit CNG volume growth.
verdicts.note: "CNG volumes grew by 17% year-on-year"; growth "coming from expanded footprint of ATGL" and "double-digit growth track record" - overall double-digit sustained (specific 12%/30% split not restated).

verdicts.item: Cheaper alternate liquid fuels (LPG/propane) are pressuring industrial PNG volumes and this stress is expected to remain.
verdicts.note: "some degrowth here and there in industrial and commercial volumes"; "hardly 1% here and there of industrial consumer" - industrial stress persists, though Q4 attributes it to the gas-price crisis rat…

verdicts.item: Zonal transmission tariff moving from 3 zones to 2; CGD PNG-home and CNG to get zone-1 tariff irrespective of distance, but final revised zone-1 tariff (currently INR42) is undecided and expected to see a moderate increase.
verdicts.note: "introduction of a simplified 2-zones transmission tariff structure from earlier 3 zones"; "zone 1 tariff, which is INR54"; "from earlier INR42 to INR54 will have an implication of INR14, around 30%."
